headline: Pretrained sequence models are steered at inference via guidance, activations, MSAs and RL objectives
label: Steering Biomolecular Language Models
summary: Preprints and papers steer pretrained biomolecular models through guidance, activations, MSAs and rewards, while benchmarks show uneven gains.
synthesis: Most items control pretrained biomolecular models without retraining the base network. GABIF guides antibody inverse-folding diffusion with a binding-affinity regressor; PredMem carries soft logit beliefs across masked co-generation steps; ARCADE applies activation engineering to codon metrics (CAI, minimum free energy, GC content); CPPainter uses RL to steer a masked-LM peptide generator; MANTA conditions IDP ensembles on language-model priors. One preprint treats MSA content as a tunable variable for generation and folding. The emphasis is on steering inputs, internal states and objectives during generation. Evidence on generality is cautionary: MLDEx benchmarks 557,143 simulated directed-evolution campaigns across 16 landscapes, and MSA Transformer features give mixed gains for enzyme recommendation.
